You're auditing provisioning automation across Nxeon's entire game-hosting catalog (Next.js/Prisma/Postgres platform, staging tree /opt/nxeon-staging for code reading — read-only investigation, report back, no code changes yet).

Goal: the owner wants game server deploys to be as close to "click pay → server is ready to play" as technically possible, with zero manual customer steps wherever avoidable. Need a complete, accurate map of where every game in the catalog currently stands.

Context already known: a prior investigation today found 6 existing games are actually **self-managed VPS products**, not managed one-click hosting — customer gets root SSH access and has to manually run SteamCMD/install the server themselves, with generic "Standard/Pro/Max" VPS pricing tiers instead of real game-specific `OsTemplate`+`GamePlan` provisioning: **ARK: Survival Evolved, Satisfactory, Project Zomboid, 7 Days to Die, V Rising, Conan Exiles**. Their wave1/wave2 seed scripts (`prisma/seed-wave1-games.ts`, `seed-wave2-games.ts`) describe a managed one-click version that was apparently written but never actually seeded (confirmed 0 `GamePlan` rows for these families on staging DB).

Your job:
1. **Enumerate the full current game catalog**: read `lib/games.ts`'s `GAME_FAMILIES` (should be 40+ entries after today's additions across wave3/4/5/6). For EACH family, determine: (a) does it have real `GamePlan` rows with a valid `osTemplateId` (i.e., genuinely one-click managed hosting), or is it VPS-only/no real GamePlan tiers (self-managed)? Query the staging DB directly (`db.gamePlan.findMany` grouped by family, or however the schema actually models the family link) rather than trusting file comments alone.
2. **For every genuinely one-click family**, check the actual provisioning path end-to-end: read the relevant `OsTemplate.setupScript` (or wherever the cloud-init/install script lives) and the `worker/` provisioning job (likely `provision()` in `worker/index.ts`) to assess: how long does this realistically take from "customer pays" to "server is joinable" (rough estimate based on what the script does — e.g. pulling a large Docker image, downloading a large SteamCMD app, etc.)? Is there ANY point where a human (Nxeon staff) needs to do something manually, or is it fully automated end-to-end?
3. **Flag any post-deploy manual customer steps** that block full "ready to play" — specifically check the newly-added games from today for known gaps: Dragonwilds' `OWNER_ID` (Steam64 ID for admin rights — check if the SERVER itself is playable without this, or if it's blocking, since admin-rights-only vs fully-blocked are very different severity), DST/TF2's Klei cluster-token/GSLT fields (same question — do these block the server from starting/being joinable, or are they admin/management niceties), and check every other new family (Soulmask, Vintage Story, Necesse, L4D2, ARK: Survival Ascended, Sunkenland, Abiotic Factor, Core Keeper, Icarus) for similar "customer-specific value with no platform default" flags in `lib/game-config.ts`.
4. **Categorize every family** into: (A) fully automated one-click, no gaps; (B) one-click but with a non-blocking manual nicety (server works, but some optional feature needs a manual step); (C) one-click but with a BLOCKING gap (server won't actually be joinable/functional without a manual step); (D) self-managed VPS only, no managed hosting exists at all (the 6 known + confirm if there are any others you find).

Report back as a clear table (game → category → specific gap if any → rough provisioning time estimate) — this is a big audit so prioritize accuracy and completeness over brevity, but keep prose commentary minimal, mostly table-driven. Under 800 words.

# Nxeon Game Catalog Provisioning Audit (staging: /opt/nxeon-staging)

## Headline finding

`lib/games.ts` `GAME_FAMILIES` has **32** entries, not 40+. Querying `GamePlan`/`OsTemplate` directly on staging DB shows only **18 families** have real rows (genuine one-click). The other **14** have **zero** `GamePlan` and **zero** `OsTemplate` rows — the wave1 (`prisma/seed-wave1-games.ts`) and wave2 (`seed-wave2-games.ts`) scripts were never actually run on staging. That's not just the "6 known" from the prior investigation — it's all 6 wave1 games **plus 7 more from wave2** (enshrouded, factorio, gmod, unturned, theforest, sonsoftheforest, bedrock) that nobody had previously flagged. `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx:194-211` confirms the deploy wizard filters `GAME_FAMILIES` down to only families with GamePlan tiers, so these 14 don't even appear in the one-click wizard — they're sold only via separate self-managed-VPS marketing pages (confirmed for v-rising, enshrouded, ark at `app/(marketing)/{v-rising,enshrouded,ark}-server-hosting/page.tsx`, explicit "self-managed VPS... you deploy yourself" copy).

**Bonus bug found**: `app/(marketing)/ark-server-hosting/page.tsx:39` markets ARK: Survival Ascended as self-managed VPS, but `arkasa` is a **separate** family that wave4 made genuinely one-click today (2026-08-31) — stale marketing copy pointing customers to the harder path for a game that no longer needs it.

## Category D — self-managed VPS only (14, zero GamePlan/OsTemplate rows)
ark, satisfactory, projectzomboid, sdtd, vrising, enshrouded (wave1), factorio, gmod, conan, unturned, theforest, sonsoftheforest, bedrock (wave2), and **schedule1** (never seeded by design — no official dedicated server binary exists at all, P2P/lobby-only; not even sold via generic VPS in any documented path).

## Categories A/B/C — the 18 genuinely one-click families

Provisioning path (`worker/index.ts` `provision()`, L423-796) is fully automated end-to-end for every one-click family with **no staff step ever required**: Proxmox clone → cloud-init → boot → SSH reachability check → **game-port health check** (`checkGamePortOpen`, blocks "ready" until the actual game port binds) → auto port-forward for NAT → DNS sync. If the game port never opens, PROVISION throws and retries/errors rather than silently reporting success (this exact bug was previously found and fixed for Terraria's TTY prompt).

| Game | Category | Gap | Rough time (pay→joinable) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minecraft | A | none | ~3-5 min |
| Valheim | A | none | ~5-8 min (SteamCMD pull) |
| Rust | A | none | ~15-30 min (~15-20GB SteamCMD) |
| Palworld | A | none | ~10-20 min (~8-10GB) |
| CS2 | A | none | ~20-40 min (~30GB dedicated files) |
| Terraria | A | none | ~3-5 min |
| Sunkenland | A | none | ~10-15 min |
| Abiotic Factor | A | none | ~10-15 min |
| Core Keeper | A | none | ~5-10 min (small download) |
| Icarus | A | none | ~15-25 min |
| ARK: Survival Ascended (arkasa) | A | none | ~30-60 min (ASA is notoriously large) |
| Soulmask | A | none | ~15-25 min |
| Vintage Story | A | none | ~5-8 min (small, non-SteamCMD) |
| Necesse | A | none | ~5-8 min |
| Left 4 Dead 2 | A | none (no GSLT field even offered) | ~15-25 min |
| RuneScape: Dragonwilds | **B** | `OWNER_ID='0'` hardcoded, **not exposed** in `lib/game-config.ts` schema at all — grants Steam64-ID admin only; server boots and is joinable without it | ~15-25 min |
| Team Fortress 2 | **B** | `SRCDS_TOKEN` (GSLT) blank by default; own help text says "required to be listed & reachable publicly" — more strongly worded than GMOD's equivalent, but Source dedicated servers historically still accept direct-IP connects without one, so treat as non-blocking pending live verification | ~15-25 min |
| Don't Starve Together | **C** | `TOKEN` (Klei cluster token) blank; `lib/game-config.ts:778` help text explicitly: **"Required to run publicly"** — customer must self-generate from their own Klei account before/after deploy. Unclear if the container even binds its UDP port without one (would fail the worker's own game-port health check and hard-error the order) — needs a live test | ~5-10 min if it starts at all |

## Bottom line
15 of 32 families are true "pay → click → play" today. 2 have minor, non-blocking manual-nicety gaps. 1 (DST) has a real customer-facing blocker baked into the newest wave. 14 are still full self-managed-VPS products with no managed path — nearly triple what the prior audit caught, because it only spot-checked 6 rather than querying `GamePlan` directly.

**Key files**: `/opt/nxeon-staging/lib/games.ts`, `/opt/nxeon-staging/lib/game-config.ts`, `/opt/nxeon-staging/worker/index.ts` (L423-796 `provision()`), `/opt/nxeon-staging/prisma/seed-wave1-games.ts`, `/opt/nxeon-staging/prisma/seed-wave2-games.ts`, `/opt/nxeon-staging/prisma/seed-wave3-games.ts`, `/opt/nxeon-staging/prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts`, `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`, `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/(marketing)/ark-server-hosting/page.tsx`.
